Lesson#11

Learning Objective: This activity aims to familiarize the students with the System’s view of management and organization.

Learning Outcome:   the students will be able distinguish between different system views and how these work in different situations.

 



Optimizing Performance Through Systems Perspectives

 



At a management summit, two managers; Suhaib Hassan; the Production Manager at Divine Cosmetics, and Muhammad Muslim, the Sales Manager at Aquapure Pharma, meet over lunch and begin a discussion about how their companies stay competitive and successful.

Suhaib Hassan says, “At Divine Cosmetics, we used to focus only on internal processes. But after a while, we noticed that our ideas were getting old and our products were not improving that led to decline in sales. Then we started working more closely with our suppliers and customers. Their suggestions helped us developing new eco-friendly organic products and increase our sales. Getting new ideas from outside really keeps our company alive and full of energy.”

Muhammad Muslim nods and replies, “We faced the same issue at Aquapure Pharma. Our sales methods were becoming outdated, so we began learning from international companies and listening to our distributors. The new ideas helped us improve our performance and stay ahead of competitors.”

Suhaib Hassan smiles and adds, “I’ve also noticed how teamwork between departments can make a big difference. When our design, production, and sales & marketing teams work together, the results are much stronger than when each department works alone.”

Muhammad Muslim agrees, “That’s true. When our sales, service, and research teams worked together on a new product idea, the final product turned out better than we expected. It really shows that companies do better when they stay connected with others and when their own departments cooperate closely. It proves the value of working as an open system.”
